narrative: Material PL2__M4BBB8ED shows moderate demand variability (CV=0.43) with 143 working-day observations spanning March 2025 to March 2026, including a statistically significant upward trend. Lead times are highly variable (CV=0.58), warranting use of the 95th-percentile effective lead time of 3.25 days. The SAP baseline carries zero safety stock, creating meaningful stockout exposure; the recommended (r,Q) policy sets safety stock at 1,446 units and an EOQ-derived order quantity of 6,431 units (capacity-constrained from 15,674), achieving the 95% service level target while reducing annual costs by approximately 85%.
warnings: EOQ capacity-constrained: unconstrained EOQ 15674 reduced to 6431 due to max_storage_units=7877.559 with safety_stock=1446.
Capacity utilization at 99.99% — storage expansion recommended to unlock further cost savings.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Moderate-variability, high-volume demand with unstable lead times and a rising trend favours a continuous-review (r,Q) model. The fixed EOQ-derived order quantity minimises total ordering and holding costs, while the reorder point r=2,759 units captures combined demand and lead-time uncertainty at 95% service level without requiring periodic review overhead.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap of 7,877.56 units binds: EOQ reduced from ~15,674 to 6,431 units, increasing ordering frequency from ~13 to ~31 orders/year and raising ordering costs. Expanding storage would reduce total costs significantly. Current policy is feasible but suboptimal relative to unconstrained EOQ.
